Senses.Explanation: Taking a seated posture (趺坐) means deliberately sitting down or taking the seat. In recorded hall scenes, Zhe'an Jingfan arranges his robe and sits before the white mallet; Huitang Zuxin takes the seat and raises the whisk; Wuzhun Shifan sits after offering incense and then speaks. The same words occur in death narration and figurative speech: Yongjue Yuanxian sits before writing his final line, while Jifei Ruyi says that he sits on his listeners’ tongues. The bare form (趺坐) does not itself state the fuller folded-leg construction explicitly written as “to sit with the legs crossed and folded” (結跏趺坐), or its contained form “cross-legged sitting” (跏趺坐); Sanshan Denglai’s verse preserves that longer wording.
